item: A redirect hop is robots-checked again when its scheme, host or path changes, and the first-run preflight's homepage ping obeys robots.txt (R636)
summary: R636 (Plan, 03:54Z, on R629's stated gaps: "Robots is re-checked, fail-closed, on any redirect hop whose robots key (scheme+host) or path changes. That covers a same-host hop to a new path and an http→https upgrade. The preflight homepage ping checks robots.txt too, with no stated exception. If robots disallows the ping or can't be fetched, the ping is skipped and reported in fixed words."). BEFORE, measured on 17576d851 over an in-memory session: R629's _take_hop_host returned early for a hop on the same host key (the host and port, no scheme), so https://a.example/x answering 302 Location /private was followed under "Disallow: /private" (requests: robots.txt, /x, /private); http://a.example/x answering 301 to https://a.example/x was followed with the https robots.txt disallowing everything, and again with it answering 500, and that robots.txt was never read (requests: the http robots.txt, /x, the https /x); a query-only hop /page?a=1 to /page?private=1 went through "Disallow: /page?private". The first-run preflight's homepage ping (src/monitoring/preflight.py) was requested after its own robots read had found disallowed, blocked (403) or http_500, and its hop from / to /en/ was followed under "Disallow: /en/". NOW (line numbers on the merged head): _take_hop_host's same-host branch (src/ingest/__init__.py:2015) calls _recheck_hop_robots (:2028) when the fetcher respects robots. It compares the hop with the address that answered by _robots_target (:2053: the robots key, scheme and host key, and the request target robots rules match, path plus ;params plus query; the fragment is never sent) and, when they differ, runs _enforce_robots(hop=True), fail-closed: RobotsDisallowed, or RobotsUnavailable with its cause, cached and backed off as a first read, the sentence ending "(reached by a redirect)" as R629's does and the address through failure_url. Another path or query on the same key is answered by the cached robots.txt (no new read); an upgrade (or a downgrade) reads the other scheme's robots.txt, under the lock the chain already holds. Same-host hops keep that lock and wait no second interval: the interval rule is per host and unchanged; the kill-switch reads R629 placed stay, and one more follows the robots check (the fold's M1). A hop to another host keeps R629's order (switch, lock handover, robots, interval, switch), and since the re-read its second read asks the epoch taken before its first (R614). _guarded_redirect_get gains hop_robots (:1837), passed by the homepage ping alone (:1971): each hop it will request (never one past the bound) is checked the same way, with no lock taken and no interval waited, as the ping takes none. Robots reads pass no chain and no hop_robots (the fetcher's _get_robots, and both preflights' own reads: preflight.py's robots read and feed_preflight.py's _check_host_robots), so a read never recurses. The ping (src/monitoring/preflight.py:149) is made only when the preflight's own read found allowed (can_fetch of the homepage) or missing (404/410); otherwise it is not requested, reachable is None (not established, never "unreachable") and homepage_skipped holds fixed words: "homepage not requested: robots.txt disallows it" for a disallow, "homepage not requested: robots.txt could not be read" for blocked (401/403), any other status and an unreachable read. A hop the ping's robots check refuses (:160) is recorded as reachable True (the homepage answered with a redirect, a 3xx, which the ping already counts as reachable) and homepage_skipped "homepage redirect not followed: robots.txt disallows the address it leads to" or "homepage redirect not followed: the robots.txt of the address it leads to could not be read"; a refusal met while the switch is engaged is skipped_offline, the preflight's rule for any check. Verdicts: robots_denied for a homepage robots.txt that disallows or is blocked, unreachable for other unreadable reads, ok otherwise, as before; and, since the fold (Steward 3's low 1), a ping whose hop is refused is never ok: robots_denied for RobotsDisallowed, unreachable for RobotsUnavailable. MERGE: built on 17576d851, then local/r629 (4c82331cc: the fold of R629's two security reads, bbd48d04b, and a row edit) merged in with no conflict. The fold's empty-path rule in _enforce_robots (an empty path checked as "/") applies to R636's re-check, so a same-host hop from /x to https://a.example?x under "Allow: /x, Disallow: /" is refused as /?x (pinned; it fails on R636 alone and on the fold alone). _robots_target adds no empty-path rule of its own: it reads "?x" and "/?x" as two targets, which costs one more cached check, never a missed one. The fold's hop_url on a hop's CrawlDelayDeferred is another host's (a same-host hop waits nothing), and its retry move after attempt += 1 leaves the retry's hop re-checked from the cache. FOLD (the two security reads, folded on 0e18d7f2e as new commits: Steward 3 GO with two lows; the independent read NO-GO on one must-fix). M1: a hop's robots check may go to the network (an upgrade's https robots.txt, another host's for the ping, a cold cache), and the hop's last switch read was its guard's, before that check. A Stop pressed while that robots.txt was read, which then answered 200 and allowed the hop, let the hop out (their probe: the upgrade and the ping's other-host and same-host hops, each requested with the switch engaged), and on a pooled keep-alive connection no socket opens for the airplane guard to see. _recheck_hop_robots (:2028) now captures kill_switch_epoch() before _enforce_robots and raises FetchFailed(KILL_SWITCH_REFUSAL) after it when kill_switch_engaged_since(epoch) (:2049): the switch engaged now, or engaged and cleared again during the check (R614). One helper where the default named two reads (_KILL.is_set(), then an epoch check): kill_switch_engaged_since is kill_switch_active() or a moved epoch, so it makes both. The page fetch raises the refusal, the ping records skipped_offline with it as the refusal, and the hop is never requested. The reads R629 placed stay where they are (its other-host branch already reads the switch after its robots read and waits; the re-read below adds the epoch to that second read), and the socket guard's own pooled-connection gap is not this fold's: src/ingest/airplane.py is untouched. LOW 1 (Steward 3): a ping whose hop was refused was verdict ok; RobotsDisallowed now gives robots_denied and RobotsUnavailable unreachable (preflight.py:167); reachable stays True and homepage_skipped keeps its words. robots, and so robots_allowed (_apply_to_metadata follows rec["robots"]), stays the source's own robots.txt read for its homepage: robots_allowed True means that robots.txt allows the homepage or is missing (404/410), False that it disallows it or refuses to be read (401/403, "blocked"), NULL that nothing was learned (unreachable, any other status). So a source can read robots_allowed True beside verdict robots_denied: its homepage is allowed and the address it redirects to is not, and the scrape-time fetcher refuses that hop regardless. A hop robots.txt answering 401/403 gives unreachable, since the fetcher files it as refused (RobotsUnavailable), never as a policy, while the homepage's own 401/403 stays blocked and robots_denied. LOW 2 / N3: a homepage robots.txt answering 401/403 (blocked) is skipped with the words "robots.txt could not be read", which is what happened, while its verdict stays robots_denied: the words describe the read, the verdict keeps the preflight's existing taxonomy (the open queue items on that verdict are docs/ledger/OPEN_QUEUE.md:14688 and C1 at :15415; the :14667 given before was wrong). N2 (the independent read): a hop's robots read is keyed and its Tor circuit named on the host key, never on the netloc as the Location wrote it (a login, or a mixed-case host with :443). The code was right, but p._replace(netloc=key) replaced by p in _recheck_hop_robots survived all 169 tests, so it is now pinned, R629's other-host line too: a circuit named on alice:hunter2@a.example is another circuit for the same host, and hands the login to the proxy. S1 (the independent read): the claim that the second-interval mutant is killed only by the https-only Crawl-delay control was wrong. On first contact with a host that declares a Crawl-delay, the first wait stamps host_schedule.json, so a second wait on the hop owes the whole delay (their probe: 7.0 s against 0); pinned for an upgrade and a new path, and the code stays. N1 (the independent read), not fixed, stated: a robots parser that raises on a body fails closed but untyped and uncached. The error escapes _get_robots as itself (only requests and fetch errors are caught there), not as RobotsUnavailable; nothing is cached, so the next fetch reads that robots.txt again; the hop is never requested; the ping records unreachable, with the error in homepage_error. A first request had it before R636. DECISIONS: a query-only change counts as a path change: Python's RobotFileParser matches the path and the query together ("Disallow: /page?private" refuses /page?private=1 and allows /page?a=1), and so are ;params; it costs no read, since the robots key is unchanged and the cached robots.txt answers. A hop whose robots key and target are both unchanged (only the fragment differs) is not checked again. The ping's homepage is judged by the preflight's own read just before it (the same URL, the same user agent, no second request); its hops by the fetcher's _enforce_robots and cache, the one a scrape uses (persisted to the robots sidecar). COSTS, stated: an http to https upgrade reads the https robots.txt once per host per TTL, also when the http robots.txt itself 301s to the https one (the cache files a read under the key asked for); a ping whose homepage redirects reads robots.txt through the fetcher once more on a cold cache (the read is persisted, and the scrape after the preflight would read it anyway); a ping refused at a hop records no homepage_status. TESTS: tests/test_redirect_robots_recheck_r636.py, 82 (67 before the fold), through the real EthicalFetcher, ingest_url, crawl_source and the preflight's _check_one, _check_host_robots and preflight_sources, over an in-memory session (every planted URL routed, so a follow is seen), a fake clock, every fetch in a bounded thread; the switch tests also on a real requests.Session over an in-memory adapter. Of the first 67, 50 fail on 4c82331cc (49 of the first 66 on 17576d851) and the 17 controls pass on both (an allowed same-host hop followed; a same-target hop not checked again; an allowed new-path, upgrade or query-only hop waiting no second interval or Crawl-delay; an upgrade not waiting a Crawl-delay only its https robots.txt declares; the hop past the bound reading nothing; a fetcher that reads no robots reading none; another host's hop reading its robots.txt once and waiting its interval; a robots read's own same-host hop not checked; a Stop as the first host answers refusing an upgrade before its robots read on a real session; the ping made when robots allows the homepage or is missing, four cases; feed_preflight's robots read following its hop with no robots read there). The fold's 15 new: 16 cases fail on 0e18d7f2e (M1's eight: the upgrade on a real and on an injected session, and the ping's other-host hop and its same-host hop on a cold cache on a real one, each with the switch engaged and with it pressed and cleared; low 1's eight: the six hop cases that now assert their verdict, a 401 case added, and a sweep's counts and metadata), and its five pins pass there (N2's three, S1's two). Three tests in tests/test_redirect_hop_robots_r629.py pinned the old behaviour (a same-host hop to a disallowed path followed; an upgrade reading no https robots.txt; the ping reading no robots.txt for the host it is redirected to) and now state R636's; they fail on 4c82331cc, the other 78 of the merged file's 81 pass there, all 81 on head. RELATED: 226 related test files (every file mentioning redirect, robots, crawl, sitemap, preflight, politeness or rate limit, R629's rule, the new file among them): on 58099bdb7 (R636 alone) 8,002 passed, 12 skipped, 4 failed; on 09c8225c8 (the merged head's code) 8,029 passed, 12 skipped, 4 failed; on c7e4d1914 (the fold's code) 8,043 passed, 12 skipped, 5 failed: the same 4, and tests/test_file_lock.py::test_an_interrupt_in_the_hold_statistic_after_the_section_leaves_nothing_held, which passed in 13 runs of 13 alone after it (a timing race in that test under a loaded machine: its helper returns once the other thread is inside the lock, which may not have released the operating-system lock yet; the fold touches no file lock). Each of the 4 fails the same way on 17576d851, the four R629 reported (tests/test_csv_feeds.py::test_feeds_api_list_and_import, KeyError 'count'; tests/test_workflow_integration.py::test_full_investigative_workflow; tests/test_shared_file_writes.py::test_no_new_unlocked_write_site_and_no_stale_allowance, the same three unlocked write sites in src/ingest/__init__.py, 426, 558 and 722, on base and head; tests/test_xdist_file_placement.py::test_a_real_run_announces_the_fixed_placement, pytest-xdist not installed here). ruff F,B,I clean on the touched files; ruff ratchet 412; mypy clean on src/ingest/__init__.py and src/monitoring/preflight.py. Mutants, in a detached worktree at 4c82331cc with head's sources (removed after), all 29 killed (28 also on 17576d851 before the merge): no same-host re-check; the re-check ignoring respect_robots; the hop compared with itself; a second interval on a same-host hop (in that round, by the Crawl-delay-only-on-https control; also by first contact with a Crawl-delay, S1); the held lock taken again (hangs); another host's hop checked twice; the comparison dropped; the target without the query, without the params, or with the fragment; the key without the scheme; the robots.txt of the address left read instead; the "(reached by a redirect)" words dropped; a forced re-read; the loop ignoring hop_robots; the ping's hop checked past the bound; robots reads recursing; the ping passing no hop_robots; the ping made whatever robots says, skipped on a disallow only, or made on a 5xx robots.txt; a skipped ping recorded as unreachable; one skip sentence for every cause; skip words carrying the state and the URL; a refused ping hop filed as a homepage error, as not reachable, or with its words swapped; a refused ping hop read before the switch; the re-check calling can_fetch itself, bypassing _enforce_robots. FOLD MUTANTS, in a detached worktree at 0e18d7f2e with the fold's sources (removed after), against the same four files: 40 of 40 killed, the 29 above and 11 new: no switch read after the hop's robots check; the read without the epoch, or the epoch captured after the check (each killed only by the four pressed-and-cleared cases); the read before the check; the refusal in other words; a same-key hop's robots read on the netloc as written (killed by the mixed-case upgrade and the login), and R629's other-host line the same way (by the mixed-case other host); a refused ping hop left ok; the hop verdicts swapped; every refused hop robots_denied; robots (so robots_allowed) set from the hop. Without -x, the second-interval mutant fails both first-contact cases and the https-only control, nothing else. RE-READ (a fresh independent read of the fold: GO on M1 and on the fold, one should-fix, two nits; Steward 3 GO on the fold). Should-fix, folded: R629's other-host branch read the switch after its robots read and its waits with _KILL.is_set() alone, so a Stop pressed and cleared again during b.example's robots read let the page fetch's hop to b.example out (the switch was clear when it went, so nothing left in airplane mode, and a first request behaves the same; but the rule above is stated for every hop). _take_hop_host now takes kill_switch_epoch() before that branch's first read and asks kill_switch_engaged_since(epoch) for its second, so a Stop pressed and cleared during the lock handover, the robots read or the waits refuses the hop. The change is in R629's branch, so it closes that path for R629's other-host hops too: every hop fetch() follows to another host (the chain is fetch()'s alone, :1469). 6 new tests (a real and an injected session, a Stop inside b.example's robots read and inside the lock handover, each engaged and pressed-and-cleared); 3 fail without the change; 3 mutants killed (no epoch, the epoch taken after the waits, the epoch taken after the handover). Nit, folded: this row said the kill-switch reads stay where R629 placed them, which the fold's M1 read had already changed. Nit, stated: a 401/403 robots.txt gives robots_denied for the homepage's own and unreachable for a hop's, a record can read reachable True beside verdict unreachable, and the summary's "robots.txt denies scraping for" warning names the source when the robots.txt that refused was another host's. NOT CHANGED, stated: the chain's interval is the first request's, read from the first address's robots.txt, so an upgrade hop does not wait a longer Crawl-delay declared only in the https robots.txt (it governs the next request asked for over https); the ping's hops take no host lock and wait no interval, as the ping never did; preflight's robots_denied verdict still holds a homepage's 401/403 beside a Disallow (the open queue items on it, docs/ledger/OPEN_QUEUE.md:14688 and C1 at :15415, are untouched). At the merge of R621 and R622 (Steward 3's note): _recheck_hop_robots runs inside R622's outer except ValueError round the redirect loop, so a ValueError raised while a hop's robots decision is taken again (no known input raises one there) is R622's FetchFailed "redirect to a URL that cannot be read, from " and the URL that answered the redirect, with no context and the hop never requested; the homepage ping records it as its homepage_error, unreachable. Pinned by 2 tests (and R629's 3 for the other-host branch). The merge also gives the ping's kill-switch read main's R614 form, kill_switch_engaged_since(epoch), where this branch read kill_switch_active(). Release-notes line: «A redirect to another page on the same site, or from http to https, is now followed only when the site's robots.txt allows the page it leads to, and the first check of each source no longer opens a homepage its robots.txt disallows or that cannot be read, nor reports a homepage that redirects to such an address as ok. (R636)»
